regressions.text: The walls and roofs of ice caves can collapse and cracks can get closed.
The Amazon is also the widest river on Earth, at times six miles wide.
The steel needle floats on top of the water because of surface tension.
On Wednesday, the United States' National Basketball Association (NBA) suspended its professional basketball season due to concerns regarding COVID-19.
Earlier the Chinese news agency Xinhua reported a plane to be hijacked.

post_mortem.why_failed: The revision added two targeted downward adjustments (a NUM–UNIT split exception and a short-identifier down-weight) that demoted previously high-scoring cut positions (notably cuts between numerals and their unit tokens and cuts after short IDs). Those demoted safe boundaries were dropped by the deterministic keeper and the next-highest (worse/contradicting) cuts were selected instead, producing the observed rise in contradiction and the rightward one-token shifts.
blamed_lines: - If the marker falls immediately between a numeral (or formatted numeric token) and an immediately adjacent measurement/unit token (examples: million, percent, kilometers, kilometer, meters, meter, miles, mile, year, years, m, km, degree), then the measured value tends to be much lower than the naive numeral bias suggests. In such NUM–UNIT splits (e.g., "1.2 <SEG> million", "240 <SEG> kilometers", "two <SEG> degree") apply a strong downward adjustment and target a low band (rough guideline: ~10–35) because single-side translation and contradiction signals frequently punish these fragments.

- If the token immediately before the marker is a short named/identifier token that translators typically copy or anchor to (examples to check for: parenthood, service, kv62, minae), then reduce the predicted score substantially (guideline target band ~15–45). Do not automatically keep such markers high merely because the token is a short name: short IDs often form part of a larger identifier or phrase whose translation depends on the following words. Exception: if the opposite side (the side after the marker when the short token is on the left) contains an independent numeral, explicit date, or measurement/unit token then the upward evidence may override this reduction.

Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward — unless the marker splits that numeral from an immediately adjacent measurement/unit token (see the NUM–UNIT split exception above), in which case bias strongly downward toward ~10–35.

Is the token immediately before the marker a short named/identifier token from the short-ID list (parenthood, service, kv62, minae)? If yes, reduce the score substantially (guideline ~15–45) unless the opposite side contains an independent numeral/date/unit that justifies a higher value.
post_mortem.lesson: Avoid blanket downward adjustments that demote cut positions which were previously high-ranked (e.g., numeral–unit or short-ID adjacencies) without checking how those removals change which boundaries survive at realistic latency budgets.
